driver-onboarding-mobile.purpose: Guide a driver through mobile identity, verification, consent, and first-use readiness with compact steps, recovery, and feedback.
useWhen: A driver must complete several mobile setup steps before operating.
Verification, consent, or device readiness can fail and recover.
The system must work as a short mobile journey rather than a desktop form.
doNotUseWithoutReview: The task is one standalone form section.
Legal consent, identity evidence, or support escalation is undefined.
The system requires product-specific routing that belongs in a template.
foundations: Uses a single-column mobile layout with stable action area.
Each step owns pending, complete, validation, and recovery states.
Short labels and helper copy avoid dense desktop instructions.
Stepper and Animated Moment communicate progress without autoplay decisions.
Keyboard, screen reader, and reduced-motion flows remain complete.
Escalation uses sheet/dialog only when the user requests help.
slots: Device trust or quick login setup.
Explains setup completion or next action.
variants: Only when recovery owner is defined.
motion: Uses Design System motion after Continue or Back.
Animated Moment is idle until the user reaches final step.
Appears inline near the current step.
accessibility: Back and Continue are reachable in the mobile action area.
Biometric setup has OTP or support fallback.
tests: Continue advances steps after user action.
Finish shows feedback only after user action.
Mobile viewport has no horizontal overflow.

canDecide: Use this pattern for mobile driver setup with verification and readiness.
Use Design System inputs, security, progress, and feedback components.
Keep each step short and recoverable.
mustAsk: Legal consent, support escalation, identity evidence, offline mode, or role assignment is unclear.
rejectIf: The system auto-advances without user action.
Desktop table/form layout is forced into mobile.
A template-level route or dashboard is hidden inside the pattern.
miel.handoff: Confirm required steps, optional skips, verification policy, consent copy, support route, and final handoff destination.
